title: Reduce 5xx spike impact: adaptive retry throttling & timeout tuning for Hosted API
creator: Priya Desai
description: Several enterprise customers reported recurring 5xx spikes and elevated end-to-end latency for the Hosted API over the last 2 weeks. Symptoms: intermittent 5xx responses from route /v1/generate, long tail timeouts, and heavy client-side retry activity from SDKs creating cascaded load. This ticket captures remediation for immediate impact reduction and the longer-term fixes: adaptive server-side retry throttling, timeout tuning for internal calls, connection pool and autoscaler configuration changes, SDK guidance and a runbook update for customer escalations.
impact_summary: Multiple paying Hosted API customers experienced degraded availability (5xx rate up to 6% for affected routes) during peak windows; support tickets escalated to SEs and account teams. The incident produced at least three high-priority escalations and one temporary credits request. Primary risk is repeated recurrence during bursty traffic without throttling and without client backoff.
root_cause_hypothesis: Investigation shows a confluence of factors: (1) delayed pod health propagation and conservative HPA scaling windows led to transient underprovisioning during sudden bursts, (2) a connection-pool exhaustion bug in runtime v1.19 caused worker threads to stall under high concurrent KV cache misses, and (3) older SDK versions used an aggressive fixed retry loop without jitter/backoff. The combination produced request queues that caused internal timeouts and 5xx errors, which then triggered more client retries and a retry storm effect.
mitigation_applied: 2026-03-02: Rolled out emergency edge-level soft quota per API key to limit concurrent inflight requests for top 10 enterprise customers (temporary rate cap)
2026-03-03: Added server-side retry budget (token-bucket) to convert naive client retries into 429 backpressure when budget exhausted
2026-03-05: Increased critical internal RPC timeouts from 20s to 45s for warmup phase, reducing premature cancellations during autoscaler spin-up
2026-03-06: Hotfix: connection pool fix deployed to runtime canary (PR #1294) — prevented socket leak under high KV miss rates
requested_changes: Implement adaptive retry throttler per-API-key with configurable SLO-preserving thresholds
Tune HPA and cluster autoscaler aggressive-scale cooldown for hosted clusters to reduce scaling lag
Add server-side metrics (retry_budget_used, inflight_by_api_key, conn_pool_waits) and dashboards
Publish SDK advisory with required backoff/jitter pattern and patch older SDK minor versions
Update customer-facing runbook and support playbooks for retry storms
acceptance_criteria: Server-side retry throttler merged and enabled behind feature flag: throttler reduces 5xx tail by at least 50% in synthetic replay tests
New dashboards show retry_budget_used and per-key inflight counts within expected ranges during a 3x synthetic burst
Runtime v1.20 contains connection pool fix and has been validated on canary for 48h with no pool-related stalls
SDK advisory published and >=90% of active customer SDKs are on patched versions within 30 days

notes: Avoid converting all 5xx to 429 globally — some internal 5xx indicate real server failure. Throttling should be policy-driven per-key and per-route.
We should measure the economic impact of throttling on top enterprise customers; coordinate with account teams before broad rollouts.
Documented SDK versions and percentage of active keys in advisory to prioritize outreach.
